trĭbūtārĭus , a, um, adj. tributum,
I.of or belonging to tribute: “necessitas,” of paying tribute, Just. 32, 2, 1 : “solum,” subject to tribute, tributary, Plin. 12, 1, 3, § 6 ; so, “praedia tributaria sunt ea, quae in his provinciis sunt, quae propriae Caesaris esse creduntur (opp. stipendiaria),” Gai. Inst. 2, 21 : “civitates,” Just. 1, 7, 2 : “Thraces Macedonum,” Flor. 3, 4, 1 : “tributarius Gallus quidam,” Suet. Aug. 40 : “causa,” concerning tribute, Dig. 49, 14, 46 : “tabellae,” letters of credit, Cic. Verr. 2, 4, 66, § 148 .
From A Latin Dictionary (Charlton T. Lewis, Charles Short, Oxford, Clarendon Press, 1879)
